notes: §1985:XVI.3.3.3 lets a MERGE in a non-independent segment name an output procedure "Totally within non-independent segments" (SR1) or "Wholly contained in a single independent segment" (SR2), and SR2's second sentence opens the rule for a MERGE in an independent segment. SortBinder.CheckSegmentation passes the OUTPUT PROCEDURE's range (procedure-name-1 THRU procedure-name-2) to Segmentation.CheckProcedures, in force only where the segment-number is an available construct (COBOL-85); RangeAllowed admits all-fixed ranges or one independent segment, which must be the statement's own when it is independent, and refuses with COBOL6877. Probes at --std 85 (classes b,c,e,f): MERGE in segment 10 with output in 20, in 49 THRU 30, in 70, in 70 THRU 70 compile and run (four merged records, IN OUT-B when THRU reaches it); 70 THRU 80, 30 THRU 70, 49 THRU 50 and segment 0 with 70 THRU 30 refused COBOL6877; at --std 2023 the segment-numbers are refused COBOL0902; an absent USING file ends the run with status 35. The witness refuses a MERGE in 60 naming 70; which procedures count is docs/CONFORMANCE.md's determination (those named, not their PERFORM closure).

next.reason: 1985: "If a MERGE statement appears in an independent segment, then any output procedure referenced by that MERGE statement must be contained"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature; independent segments are absent, so no candidate states this restriction". The rule restricts output procedures relative to independent segments. No 2023 clause holds segmentation, and the MERGE syntax rule (SR-14.9.24.3-1) does not mention segments.
